s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive ataxia with spasms and myoclonus
key_facts: Difficulty with gait progressed after cessation of alcohol use
Throat spasms do not affect speech or eating
Patient unable to stop palatal myoclonus with voluntary muscle use
Normal genetic testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12
Severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy on MRI brain without contrast

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive ataxia with spasms and myoclonus
key_facts: Difficulty with gait progressed after cessation of alcohol use
Throat spasms do not affect speech or eating
Patient unable to stop palatal myoclonus with voluntary muscle use
Normal genetic testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12
Severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy on MRI brain without contrast

shortlist.label: Multiple system atrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive ataxia, autonomic dysfunction, and parkinsonian features

shortlist.label: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 7
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive ataxia and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy

shortlist.label: Palatal myoclonus syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Palatal myoclonus at 1-2 Hz and inability to suppress with voluntary muscle use

shortlist.label: Dentatorubral-pallidoluysian atrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive ataxia, myoclonus, and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy

shortlist.label: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive ataxia, myoclonus, and severe cerebral atrophy

raw.rationale: The combination of progressive ataxia, autonomic dysfunction (implied by severe atrophy and progressive symptoms), bradykinesia, and mild rigidity, along with the presence of palatal myoclonus, points towards Multiple System Atrophy (MSA), which is characterized by a combination of cerebellar ataxia, parkinsonism, and autonomic dysfunction.

rejected.label: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 7
rejected.why: Genetic testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12 was normal, and while type 7 was not explicitly tested, the broader clinical presentation including parkinsonian features and severe atrophy is more suggestive of MSA

rejected.label: Palatal myoclonus syndrome
rejected.why: While palatal myoclonus is present, it is part of a broader neurological decline including ataxia, bradykinesia, and rigidity, suggesting a more complex disorder like MSA rather than a syndrome primarily characterized by myoclonus

rejected.label: Dentatorubral-pallidoluysian atrophy
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a combination of myoclonus, epilepsy, and dementia, which are not the primary features in this case

rejected.label: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease
rejected.why: The disease progression over 20 years is not typical for Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, which usually has a much shorter duration of illness
